description: The line plot illustrates the accuracy (ACC, in percentage) of five different methods—Base, MEND, FT, MEMIT, and ROME—across varying co-occurrence numbers, with the x-axis representing the co-occurrence number on a logarithmic scale ranging from 1 to 1000, and the y-axis showing accuracy from 60% to 80%. The Base method, represented by black circles connected by a solid line, shows a steady increase in accuracy from approximately 62.5% at a co-occurrence number of 1 to around 67.5% at 1000. The MEND method, shown with brown diamonds and a solid line, starts at about 68% and rises to roughly 76.5%. The FT method, indicated by blue triangles and a solid line, begins at approximately 64% and increases to about 69.5%. The MEMIT method, marked by purple circles and a solid line, starts at around 67% and climbs to about 75%. The ROME method, represented by green squares and a solid line, exhibits the highest accuracy, starting at approximately 74% and increasing to around 81%. All methods demonstrate a general upward trend in accuracy as the co-occurrence number increases, with ROME consistently achieving the highest accuracy across all values.
